name: Mistral Vibe

surfaces.label: Mistral Vibe VS Code extension (publisher mistralai, id mistralai.mistral-vibe-code): runs the bundled Vibe agent as an ACP subprocess. INFERRED path: the docs say the agent is built in, but the bundled binary's name and folder were not inspected (extension not installed, VSIX not fetched). Also matches the same extension inside VS Code forks that use ~/.<fork>/extensions/

vibe-acp or vibe-app-server as a standalone PyInstaller binary (Zed downloads vibe-acp-darwin-<arch>-<ver>.tar.gz and runs ./vibe-acp; vibe-app-server is the same packaging, used by desktop clients). Hosts many sessions, not one. Vetoes the pty helper: a frozen vibe-app-server re-runs itself as 'vibe-app-server --internal-posix-pty-helper <fds>' for each shell command (vibe/app_server/entrypoint.py handles that flag), which would otherwise show up as a second session
vibe-acp (Agent Client Protocol server) from uv tool, pipx or pip: a python interpreter running .../bin/vibe-acp. Started by Zed, JetBrains, Neovim (avante) or the VS Code extension. Never retitled

vibe-app-server (JSON-RPC over stdio) from uv tool, pipx or pip: a python interpreter running .../bin/vibe-app-server. Child of the Rust TUI (VIBE_CLI=rust); also started by desktop clients. Never retitled

Rust TUI, opt-in with the undocumented env var VIBE_CLI=rust: the python launcher execs .../site-packages/vibe/_bin/vibe-rs in place, so argv[0] is that path and the name is vibe-rs. Its agent runs in a direct child, vibe-app-server. The child is started as 'vibe-app-server --experimental-harness' (DEFAULT_APP_SERVER_ARGS), so a Rust TUI session always uses the unified store

Python TUI, the default. After startup the process retitles itself with setproctitle to 'Vibe CLI', so ps shows 'Vibe CLI' and argv[0] splits to 'Vibe'; the original python path and every flag (including --resume <id>) are gone from the command line. Applies to every subcommand (vibe -p, vibe mcp, vibe --setup, vibe update), which are short-lived. Retitle effect on macOS ps is INFERRED from source, not seen

Python TUI before setproctitle has run, or if it failed: python interpreter with the console script .../bin/vibe as argument (uv tool: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/bin/python ~/.local/bin/vibe). Short window at startup. Excludes the pty helper child the unified harness spawns for shell commands
Vibe Code Web (remote sandbox on a GitHub repo, reached from the CLI with /teleport). Nothing runs on the Mac

session_store.glob_note: Legacy Python harness layout. Folder name is <session_prefix>_<UTC YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_<first 8 chars of session id>, with meta.json beside messages.jsonl. per_session matches only when {session_id} is the 8-character short id (what the resume picker shows), not a full uuid. The Unified Harness, which the vibe_cli_unified_harness_rollout experiment (and --experimental-harness) switches on and which the wheel bundles since 2.25.6, writes a different layout instead: ~/.vibe/logs/session/unified/<full session id>/{CURRENT, journal/<16 digits>.jsonl, chunks/}. Which layout a given Mac uses is decided per user by a server-side flag, so check both globs.
session_store.home_override: VIBE_HOME moves ~/.vibe. session_logging.save_dir in config.toml moves logs/session. MISTRAL_VIBE_SESSION_ROOT is read by the unified host only.

pid_index.note: Not in the schema. Maps a live pid to its session without argv, which matters because the Python TUI erases its own argv and a fresh launch never carries an id.
pid_index.lease_diagnostic: ~/.vibe/logs/session/active/<session id>.lock.json  keys: lease_version, session_id, process_id, acquired_at. Written next to an flock-held <id>.lock. Both files are unlinked on clean release; after a crash the diagnostic can remain, so check process_id is alive. The unified store uses the same files.
pid_index.meta_json_keys: session_id, parent_session_id, start_time, end_time, git_commit, git_branch, environment, origin_directory, username, child_sessions, loops, title, title_source, bumped_at, pinned_at, archived_at, unseen_at, seen_at, experiments, config, import_provenance, created_worktree, plus stats, total_messages, last_message_fingerprint, tools_available, agent_profile, system_prompt written on save. Names taken from the SessionMetadata type and the save code, not read from a file.
pid_index.messages_jsonl_keys: role, content, images, injected, reasoning_content, reasoning_payloads, reasoning_message_id, tool_calls, name, tool_call_id, tool_result, message_id, user_display_content, input_text, resources, manual_shell, context_boundary. Names from the LLMMessage type, not read from a file.

working_signals.meaning: Legacy Python harness only. The bash tool, a hook command, a manual '!cmd' and the update check each run as a DIRECT child of the TUI: asyncio create_subprocess_shell with executable=$SHELL. CORRECTED: argv[0] is $SHELL, not sh, so ps shows '/bin/zsh -c <cmd>' (name zsh) on a default macOS account; only an unset $SHELL gives sh. Both are in the probe's SHELLS set, a non-POSIX $SHELL (nu, xonsh) is not. Idle MCP stdio servers are not shells, so they do not trip it. Blind in four cases: a single simple command (no ';', '&&' or pipe) is exec'd in place by zsh and bash -c, so the shell disappears and the direct child is the command itself (seen locally with zsh, see sources); the Unified Harness puts a python pty helper between the TUI and the shell (direct child is python, shell is a grandchild); the Rust TUI's tools run under vibe-app-server, a grandchild; and any turn that is only streaming a model reply or waiting on the network. Inferred from source, never observed.

Legacy layout only unless the unified glob is used. messages.jsonl is appended when the user prompt is accepted, after each completed model step (once its tool calls have run) and in a finally block when the turn ends. Nothing is written while a reply streams or a long tool runs, so a quiet file does not mean idle. Needs a session id, which a fresh launch does not have in argv; map through the lease diagnostic instead.

Inferred, not measured. The Textual UI animates a spinner and re-renders streamed text during a turn. For the Rust TUI the tree includes the vibe-app-server child, so the sum still covers the agent. A turn waiting on the network burns no CPU.

waiting_signals.meaning: OSC 0 title, default on (experimental_enable_tab_status = true), Python and Rust TUI alike. '>> <title>' while a turn is running, '? <title>' while an approval or a question is pending, plain '<title>' idle (title is the session title, else 'Vibe'). When the terminal is unfocused and a bell fired, the title becomes '<title> - Action Required' or '<title> - Task Complete' instead. The precise turn signal, and the only wait signal, but it lives in the terminal host (tmux 3.7+, cmux), not in ps. Off when the user sets experimental_enable_tab_status = false; not written under --headless.
Terminal bell on 'action required' and on 'task complete', only while the terminal is unfocused, throttled to 1 per second. enable_notifications, default true. No file or process trace.
For ACP hosts (Zed, JetBrains, VS Code extension) the agent sends this JSON-RPC request to the client when a tool needs approval. Visible to the client only, not to another process.

Hooks have no wait event. pre_tool fires BEFORE the permission prompt, so it cannot tell 'asking' from 'running'. post_tool does not fire when the user denies or the tool never ran. post_agent fires when a model reply ends with no pending tool calls, which marks the end of a turn but not a wait.

hooks.config: hooks.toml with [[hooks]] tables: ~/.vibe/hooks.toml (user, loaded second) and <project>/.vibe/hooks.toml (project, loaded first, trusted folders only; a project entry beats a user entry with the same name). No flag needed. Fields: name, type, command, match (pre_tool/post_tool only), timeout (default 60 s), strict, description. Payload arrives as JSON on stdin with session_id, parent_session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name (+ tool fields). Exit 0 with empty stdout = pass. Subagents inherit the parent's hooks. Shell commands, not plugin code.

telemetry.how: config.toml: enable_otel = true (default false) AND enable_telemetry = true (default true). OTLP over HTTP to <otel_endpoint>/v1/traces, or by default to Mistral's own telemetry endpoint using the provider API key; standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables add auth for a custom collector. Any config field can also be set as a VIBE_<FIELD> env var. Spans for agent (invoke_agent), model and tool (execute_tool) operations, gen_ai semantic conventions, conversation id as baggage; client-side redaction otel_redaction = default|strict|none. BatchSpanProcessor, so spans leave in batches after they end: not a live signal for a monitor. Only the legacy and app-server paths call setup_tracing (vibe/app_server/_runtime.py).

sources.claim: setproctitle does change what macOS ps shows, provided the native module loads. When it does not load (a corrupt conda install), the call silently does nothing and ps keeps the original argv, which the pre-retitle python surface then matches.
sources.evidence: https://github.com/dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle/issues/128: with a working install setproctitle('Test') gave ps '14442 ttys002 0:00.03 Test' on macOS 13 (Apple Silicon, v1.2.3); a project contributor reports 'everything works fine' on macOS 13.2 Intel python.org 3.10; with a broken conda .so the same call left 'python testscript.py'. Issue closed as a conda problem. https://github.com/dvarrazzo/py-setproctitle README lists MacOS X as supported. Not tested with 1.3.7 or with Vibe itself.

sources.claim: Shell tool children: argv[0] of the direct child is $SHELL (not sh), and a lone simple command is exec'd in place so the shell is absent from ps.
sources.evidence: python3 -c "subprocess.Popen('sleep 2; true', shell=True, executable='/bin/zsh')" then ps -o args= -p <pid> -> '/bin/zsh -c sleep 2; true'; the same with the single command 'sleep 2' -> 'sleep 2'. Vibe passes executable=os.environ.get('SHELL') to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell in vibe/core/utils/shell.py::spawn_shell_command, which uses subprocess.Popen(shell=True) semantics.

notes: Never run against a live instance. (1) The default Python TUI erases its own command line: ps shows 'Vibe CLI', so the flags, --resume <id> and even -p are invisible, and a one-shot 'vibe -p' run cannot be told from a TUI by argv (a -p run is working for its whole life). The row matches 'Vibe' + 'CLI' for that reason; the pre-retitle python shape is a second, short-lived surface. Map pid to session through ~/.vibe/logs/session/active/<id>.lock.json (process_id). Short-lived subcommands (vibe mcp, vibe update, vibe --setup) get the same title and briefly show up as idle sessions. (2) Strongest signal is the OSC 0 title (>> running, ? waiting) which needs the terminal host, not ps. From ps alone only three weak signals exist: a direct sh child (legacy harness), a fresh messages.jsonl, and CPU. There is no sleep inhibitor, no hook for permission waits, and no turn-start hook. (3) Two session layouts: legacy session_*/messages.jsonl and unified unified/<id>/journal/*.jsonl; a server-side flag decides. (4) Rust TUI (VIBE_CLI=rust; its app-server child is always started with --experimental-harness, so it uses the unified store and the lease pid is the CHILD's pid, not vibe-rs's): vibe-rs plus a vibe-app-server child; the probe skips a child whose parent matches, so the child is folded into vibe-rs and its tool shells are grandchildren, invisible to tool_children. (5) vibe-acp and vibe-app-server host several sessions per process (editors, desktop): one process is not one session. (6) The lease files exist only while session_logging.enabled is true (default). Vibe Desktop and the VS Code extension's bundled binary could not be inspected; their surfaces are inferred or absent. (7) The names python/python3/Python in the interpreter surfaces are generic; they are held safe only by the bin/vibe-acp, bin/vibe-app-server and /bin/vibe argument requirements, and '/bin/vibe' is a substring test, so it also matches any python script whose path contains /bin/vibe (bin/vibe.py, bin/vibecoder, bin/vibe-kanban); the window is short unless setproctitle failed. (8) A PyInstaller build of the TUI (release asset vibe-<os>-<arch>-<ver>.zip, contains an executable named vibe) has no surface: the name 'vibe' is too generic to match alone, and it retitles to 'Vibe CLI' after start anyway. (9) Homebrew installs (formula 2.25.0, python@3.14) run as a venv python and are covered by the interpreter surfaces. Shell tool children show as the user's $SHELL (zsh), and a single simple command has no shell at all, so tool_children under-reports.
